Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A generic institutional records office files ordinary paperwork through dated intake registers, routed forms, and sequential document numbering. Each entry records a submission, an associated field value, and the required approval check before filing. Entries are retained as filed and referenced by record number and date.

2) What occurred: On the dated intake record, the actor logged the component replacement while the conformity certificate field remained unverified. On the next dated entry, the actor recorded the installation on the airworthiness form while the traceability check stayed unverified. On the following dated entry, the actor filed the part history under an existing serial number while the source document field stayed unverified. On the final dated entry, the actor submitted the package for approval while the sign-off field stayed unverified.

3) Materials/access observed: The actor accessed the maintenance log file, the airworthiness form document, the part history register, and the approval routing channel. The actor used a named account with write access to all four records.

4) Indicators & artifacts: The artifacts include four dated entries in the maintenance log file, one airworthiness form document, one part history register entry, and one routing submission in the approval channel. The field values show a component identifier mismatch, a duplicate serial number reference, a missing conformity certificate attachment, and an approval submitted without a completed sign-off.
